database_summary: University course scheduling schema (SQLite) containing entities for classrooms, departments, courses, instructors, students, sections, time slots, advisors and relationships for teaching assignments, enrollments (takes) and prerequisites. The model mixes descriptive master/entity tables (department, course, classroom, instructor, student, time_slot) with event/history-like tables (section, teaches, takes, advisor, prereq). Keys in many relationship tables are composite across course/section/semester/year, but the DDL declares multiple PRIMARY KEY columns per table (SQLite permits a single PRIMARY KEY but the provided DDL lists multiple columns; treat the listed columns as the intended composite keys).

accepted.name: section_with_course_instructor_room_time
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id AS course_id,
  s.sec_id AS sec_id,
  s.semester AS semester,
  s.year AS year,
  s.building AS building,
  s.room_number AS room_number,
  s.time_slot_id AS time_slot_id,
  c.title AS title,
  c.dept_name AS dept_name,
  c.credits AS credits,
  t.ID AS ID,
  i.name AS name,
  i.dept_name AS instructor_dept_name,
  cl.capacity AS capacity,
  ts.day AS day,
  ts.start_hr AS start_hr,
  ts.start_min AS start_min,
  ts.end_hr AS end_hr,
  ts.end_min AS end_min
FROM section s
LEFT JOIN course c
  ON s.course_id = c.course_id
LEFT JOIN teaches t
  ON s.course_id = t.course_id
  AND s.sec_id = t.sec_id
  AND s.semester = t.semester
  AND s.year = t.year
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON t.ID = i.ID
LEFT JOIN classroom cl
  ON s.building = cl.building
  AND s.room_number = cl.room_number
LEFT JOIN time_slot ts
  ON s.time_slot_id = ts.time_slot_id
accepted.description: One row per section offering enriched with course title/credits, instructor(s) assigned, classroom info and time slot details. Useful when answering questions about offerings, who teaches them, where/when they meet, or joining to enrollments or grades. | Use for: List sections with instructor and room/time details; Which instructor teaches a given section or course offering; Where and when is a section held and what is the classroom capacity; Join sections to enrollments or grades

accepted.name: takes_with_student_course_section
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tk.ID AS ID,
  s.name AS name,
  s.dept_name AS dept_name,
  s.tot_cred AS tot_cred,
  tk.course_id AS course_id,
  tk.sec_id AS sec_id,
  tk.semester AS semester,
  tk.year AS year,
  tk.grade AS grade,
  c.title AS title,
  c.credits AS credits,
  t.ID AS instructor_ID,
  i.name AS instructor_name
FROM takes tk
LEFT JOIN student s
  ON tk.ID = s.ID
LEFT JOIN course c
  ON tk.course_id = c.course_id
LEFT JOIN teaches t
  ON tk.course_id = t.course_id
  AND tk.sec_id = t.sec_id
  AND tk.semester = t.semester
  AND tk.year = t.year
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON t.ID = i.ID
accepted.description: One row per student enrollment (takes) with student demographic info and course/section metadata (title, credits, semester/year, instructor if any). Use for grade reports, per-student transcripts, or course-level enrollment analyses. | Use for: Student transcript / grades per term; Which students took a given course offering; Combine enrollment with instructor to see which instructor taught which students

accepted.name: course_prereq_edges
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.course_id AS course_id,
  p.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq p
accepted.description: One row per direct prerequisite edge (course -> prereq). Use as the base edge set for recursive traversal to find full prerequisite chains or to detect cycles. | Use for: Compute full prerequisite chains via recursive traversal; Detect cycles in course prerequisites; Find all immediate prerequisites for a course

accepted.name: instructor_salary_by_department
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(ID) AS instructor_count,
  AVG(salary) AS avg_salary,
  MIN(salary) AS min_salary,
  MAX(salary) AS max_salary,
  SUM(salary) AS total_salary
FROM instructor
GROUP BY dept_name
accepted.description: Department-level aggregates of instructor counts and salary measures (count, avg_salary, min_salary, max_salary, total_salary). Useful for budgeting, staffing and pay-distribution questions. | Use for: Compare departments by instructor headcount or total/avg salary; Detect departments with unusually high/low average pay; Budget planning based on instructor salaries

accepted.name: course_offering_counts_by_term
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  course_id AS course_id,
  semester AS semester,
  year AS year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sec_id) AS sections_offered
FROM section
GROUP BY course_id, semester, year
accepted.description: Counts of distinct section offerings per course per semester/year. Use to find how often a course is offered, trending offer frequency, or to join with enrollment counts. | Use for: How many sections of a course were offered in a term; Identify courses with growing/shrinking offering counts; Prepare denominator for enrollment per-section metrics

accepted.name: student_enrollment_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tk.ID AS ID,
  COUNT(*) AS enrollments_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tk.course_id) AS distinct_courses_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tk.semester || '_' || tk.year) AS distinct_terms_count
FROM takes tk
GROUP BY tk.ID
accepted.description: Per-student counts of enrollments and distinct courses taken, plus number of distinct semesters attended. Useful for student activity summaries, retention metrics, or filtering active students. | Use for: How many courses a student has taken; Identify inactive students by term counts; Prepare per-student cohorts for advising

accepted.name: instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ID AS ID,
  t.course_id AS course_id,
  t.sec_id AS sec_id,
  t.semester AS semester,
  t.year AS year,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.ID ORDER BY t.year DESC, t.semester DESC) AS teaching_rank
FROM teaches t
accepted.description: Per-instructor chronological ranking of the sections they taught, ordered by year then semester. Exposes a rank so callers can select the most recent or top-N taught sections per instructor. | Use for: Find most recent sections taught by an instructor (WHERE teaching_rank = 1); Top-N recent courses per instructor; Temporal analysis of instructor workload

accepted.name: student_latest_advisor
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.s_ID AS s_ID,
  a.i_ID AS i_ID,
  i.name AS name
FROM advisor a
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON a.i_ID = i.ID
accepted.description: One row per student with their advisor ID and advisor name. Useful for routing advising communications or joining advisor attributes to student cohorts. | Use for: Lookup advisor for a given student; List advisors and their advisees; Join advisor info into student-level reports

accepted.name: time_slot_readable
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  time_slot_id AS time_slot_id,
  day AS day,
  start_hr AS start_hr,
  start_min AS start_min,
  end_hr AS end_hr,
  end_min AS end_min,
  printf('%02d:%02d', start_hr, start_min) AS start_time_text,
  printf('%02d:%02d', end_hr, end_min) AS end_time_text
FROM time_slot
accepted.description: Normalized time_slot with a human-readable start/end time strings. Use when presenting schedules or grouping by time ranges. Preserves original time components for analytical joins. | Use for: Display readable meeting times for schedules; Group sections by start time or time window; Filter time slots by human-readable range

accepted.name: course_popularity_by_enrollment
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tk.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(*) AS total_enrollments,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tk.ID) AS distinct_students
FROM takes tk
GROUP BY tk.course_id
accepted.description: Per-course aggregate enrollments across all terms: total enrollments and distinct student count. Useful for ranking course popularity, planning capacity, or identifying high-demand courses. | Use for: Which courses have the highest enrollment historically; Prepare inputs for capacity planning and course offering frequency; Identify courses with many unique students vs repeat enrollments
